items.title: Which metric axiom list this library uses, the live naming fork between semimetric and pseudometric, and why extended metrics are not treated here
Under dependent choice a locally compact Hausdorff space is completely regular, hence Tychonoff
Under choice, $c(X)\le d(X)\le w(X)$ and $\chi(X),L(X)\le w(X)$
Under the ultrafilter lemma and Dependent Choice, a Tychonoff space is $G_\delta$ in some Hausdorff compactification exactly when it is $G_\delta$ in every one
The covers admitting an open refinement form a compatible uniform-cover structure on a nonempty compact Hausdorff space; in particular every open cover is uniform
For a metric space with its metric topology, compactness in the topological sense is compactness in the metric sense, and the two notions of compact subset coincide
Under Dependent Choice, every completely metrizable subspace of a metric space is $G_\delta$
A map of topological spaces is continuous at a point if and only if it preserves every net converging to that point
Every countably based uniformity is generated by one pseudometric, which is a metric exactly when the uniformity is separated
$\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n \ge 1$ with the Euclidean metric are complete, componentwise from the Cauchy criterion in $\mathbb{R}$
If $(Y,d)$ is complete then $Y^{X}$ is complete in the uniform metric, and so is $C(X,Y)$
A space is Hausdorff if and only if its diagonal is closed in the square carrying the product topology
Lattice Stone–Weierstrass theorem on a compact Hausdorff space
Lipschitz equivalence implies uniform equivalence implies topological equivalence
A point is a cluster point of a net if and only if some subnet converges to it
For a Hausdorff space, paracompactness is equivalent, under choice and dependent choice, to the existence of a locally finite subordinate partition of unity for every open cover
$T_0$, $T_1$, $T_2$, regularity, $T_3$, complete regularity, and Tychonoffness are productive

A uniformly continuous map from a dense subspace into a complete metric space extends uniquely to a uniformly continuous map on the whole space

candidate_diagrams.claim: The Klein bottle is the square quotient with (x,0)~(x,1) and (0,y)~(1,1-y); the four corners form one vertex class and a disk neighborhood.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The two identifications, reversal on the vertical pair, and corner-class cycle are spatial gluing data that are much easier to read on a square than from the relations alone.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw one unit square; identify bottom/top with matching arrows and left/right with reversed arrows; label the four corner identifications and the one-polygon boundary word aba^{-1}b. Keep the square as quotient data and do not draw an embedded Klein bottle in R^3.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible; source-supported; not required for definition or proof

candidate_diagrams.claim: The cylinder glues (0,y) to (1,y), while the Mobius band glues (0,y) to (1,1-y); the cylinder is identified with (R/Z)×[0,1].
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The only change between the two constructions is the reversal in the edge-pairing map, and the cylinder homeomorphism is given by explicit quotient maps. A paired square diagram makes the exact relation and map visible.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show two squares with left and right edges marked; use same-direction arrows for the cylinder and reversed arrows for the Mobius band. For the cylinder panel, include the quotient projection P_c and the induced map to (R/Z)×[0,1]. Label as a gluing comparison only; the item explicitly does not claim these spaces are different or identify an invariant for distinguishing them.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, strongly source-supported; not required for proof validity

candidate_diagrams.claim: For fixed n, r_n:H→C_n is the identity on C_n and maps every other circle C_m to the common point 0.
candidate_diagrams.kind: retraction map on a convergent circle family
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The definition of H is a nested visual family of tangent circles, and the piecewise map has a distinct geometric action on one chosen circle versus all remaining circles. A diagram gives the map a concrete domain/range and fixed-point set.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw finitely many circles C_m tangent at 0 with radii 1/m, highlight C_n, and show r_n fixing every point of C_n while sending each other circle to 0; label that r_n|C_n=id and r_n(C_m)={0} for m≠n. Indicate the omitted tail accumulates at 0.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, source-supported; the map remains fully defined in prose

candidate_diagrams.claim: The quotient q:R→R/Z is evenly covered over open intervals I of length below 1 by the pairwise disjoint translates I+k; integer translations are exactly the deck maps.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The local covering condition is a literal family of disjoint interval lifts and the global deck action is generated by translations; a line-to-circle map with lifts shows the maps and relation exactly.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw q:R→R/Z with one open arc q[I] and its preimage as disjoint intervals I+k, k∈Z, each mapping homeomorphically to that arc; label deck transformations τ_n(x)=x+n and q∘τ_n=q. Preserve that I is open and length <1.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, strongly source-supported; not required for proof validity

candidate_diagrams.claim: H(x,t)=((1−t)+t/||x||₂)x deforms R^n\{0} onto S^{n−1}, fixes the sphere pointwise, and never reaches 0.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The central statement is a parameterized homotopy along rays, including initial/final maps, a fixed subset, and exclusion of the origin. One low-dimensional schematic would make these map relations immediate.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: In a schematic R² slice, draw the unit circle, a nonzero x on a ray, and the segment traced by H(x,t) from x to x/||x||₂; mark every sphere point fixed for all t and the origin excluded. Label H(x,0)=x and H(x,1)=x/||x||₂. Mark the picture as schematic for n≥1, not as a proof of continuity.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, strongly source-supported; not required for proof validity
